title: Two-way secret-key capacity of the qubit amplitude-damping channel
source: The question was supplied by the contributor. Its literature basis is the amplitude-damping capacity bounds of Pirandola, Laurenza, Ottaviani, and Banchi, arXiv v8, Eq.~(48) and Supplementary Note~5 \sourcecite{ref:adkey-plob}{PLOB17}. Harney and Pirandola explicitly identify the exact amplitude-damping capacity as unknown in Sec.~IV~A~1, immediately after Eqs.~(25)--(26) \sourcecite{ref:adkey-harney}{HP22}.

comment: The remaining problem is the exact value of $K(\mathcal A_p)$ for $0<p<1$. The related record \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_e490c9462b37a548/}{Two-way quantum capacity: amplitude-damping channel} asks for the two-way quantum capacity $Q_2(\mathcal A_p)$; although $Q_2\le K$, equality is not assumed, and bounds proved only for entanglement transmission do not automatically bound secret-key generation. The unassisted private capacity is also a different quantity. Literature audit: 8 September 2026. Primary passages in the cited papers were checked, and searches for later exact-capacity results through accessible arXiv and publisher pages found no resolution; this was not an exhaustive citation-index search.
